The embedding operator $\iota_{a \leftarrow b}: L_2^b \to L_2^a$ maps a signal by appending zeros, e.g., $\iota_{n \leftarrow p}(f) = (f_1, \dots, f_p, 0, \dots, 0)^\top \in L_2^n$. The projection operator $\pi_{a \leftarrow b}: L_2^b \to L_2^a$ maps a signal by truncation, e.g., $\pi_{p \leftarrow n}(f) = (f_1, \dots, f_p)^\top \in L_2^p$. This embedding avoids conservatism by restricting the input space.
